newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council to debate two consumer complaint laws.
newsitem.headline: Council to debate two consumer complaint laws.

text.p: The Consumer Council will discuss two documents on Monday aimed at making it easier for consumers to pursue complaints about goods and services bought in another EU member state, making the EU single market more consumer-friendly.

The two papers are the draft directive on injuctions for the protection of consumer interests and the communication on a plan of action on consumer access to justice and the settlement of consumer disputes.
In the absence of the European Parliament's opinion the Council will only hold an orientation debate on the proposed directive on injunctions for the protection of consumer interests.
The plan is for designated national organisations to take up individual consumer complaints.
Diplomats said on Friday the debate will cover the scope of the directive and in particular whether it should cover both individual and collective interests of consumers.

The ministers will also examine how infringements of EU directives transposed by member states should be dealt with and whether it should cover infringements of a national as well as transnational nature and whether it should cover both consumer and industrial interests.
It will also discuss the designation of competent courts and which bodies should be designated to initiate actions to pursue individuals' complaints.

As regards the Commission Communication on an action plan on consumer access to justice and the settlement of consumer disputes, the Council will discuss draft conclusions which generally back the Commission's line that out of court settlements should be promoted to avoid what could be prohibitive costs of lawsuits.
It also wants to establish a common EU form to facilitate access to court procedures.
